evidence.claim: Chinese-language AI-native engine for end-to-end novel creation from inspiration to full book, beginner-oriented, agent-driven workflows with review/repair/state feedback; available as Windows desktop app.

Shipped baseline: Electron desktop shell, chapter state machine (plan/draft/review/revise/finalize), real word-count gate (model self-reported counts not trusted), tool-call-only chapter delivery, checkpoint resume, local project folder persistence to Markdown/TXT, controlled web search (off by default) with untrusted snapshots, OpenAI-compatible providers (DeepSeek/MiMo presets), cost/cache reporting, skill runtime, Windows packaging.

recommendations.statement: Position WWriting as 'local-first, verifiable-delivery desktop agent for long-form fiction': data lives in the user's own folder as Markdown/TXT; delivery is machine-verified (real word count, tool-call commits, checkpoints).
recommendations.acceptance_signal: README first screen states both differentiators (local data ownership, verifiable delivery) within 5 seconds of reading; a competitor comparison table appears in the README.

recommendations.statement: Add an editable story bible (characters/settings/foreshadowing) persisted as Markdown files inside the project folder, auto-injected during drafting.
recommendations.acceptance_signal: A user can maintain a character card in the UI and see it injected into draft prompts; after restart the card remains as an ordinary file openable in any editor.

recommendations.statement: Build a skill ecosystem: export/import skill packs (continuation, style, suspense hooks) as shareable zips on top of the existing skill runtime.
recommendations.acceptance_signal: A skill authored by one user can be exported, imported by another user, and used without code changes.
